description:
The expert talk on Malware Detection proved to be an effective academic activity for Semester 6 students studying Cryptography and Network Security (IT348). It successfully reinforced theoretical knowledge while promoting practical understanding of malware behavior and network defense strategies. Such activities play a crucial role in preparing students for advanced studies, research, and professional roles in cybersecurity. 

 After participating in this event, students were able to: 
 1. Understand core security principles such as the CIA Triad and their role in protecting networked systems.
 2. Identify common malware types and behaviours, including persistence mechanisms and fileless attacks.
 3. Recognize indicators of compromise (IoCs) at both host and network levels.
 4. Analyze real-world attack scenarios and select appropriate defensive and response actions.
 5. Apply incident response concepts, including containment, eradication, and lessons learned.
 6. Appreciate the importance of layered security architectures and proactive threat detection.

 The expert talk made several significant contributions to student learning:
 • Practical Exposure: Students gained hands-on insight into how theoretical security concepts manifest in real cyber incidents.
 • Critical Thinking Development: Scenario-based questions enhanced analytical and decision-making skills.
 • Industry Relevance: Exposure to modern attack techniques aligned academic learning with current cybersecurity trends.
 • Security Awareness: It strengthened awareness of common mistakes in incident handling and the importance of timely response.

description:

title: Expert session on Vibration Measurement
description: The expert session on Vibration Measurement was organized by CHAMOS Matrusanstha, Department of Mechanical Engineering, CSPIT for undergraduate students of B.Tech Mechanical Engineering branch on 20th February, 2026. Dr. Sebin Jose from HILTI Manufacturing India, was invited to conduct the session. Dr. Sebin began by establishing the fundamentals of vibration, transitioning into practical measurement methodologies and the specific instrumentation required for data collection. A significant portion of the session focused on the accelerometer, the industry standard for capturing vibration data. Dr. Sebin detailed the critical process of sensor selection, emphasizing that the choice must align with the machine's frequency range and environmental conditions. He also highlighted that mounting techniques—whether using studs, magnets, or adhesives—directly impact the accuracy of the high-frequency signals captured. The session concluded by framing vibration analysis as a cornerstone of Condition Monitoring. By interpreting vibration signatures, maintenance teams can detect early signs of wear, such as imbalance or bearing failure, allowing for proactive repairs before catastrophic breakdowns occur.

title: Expert Talk - Digital Electronics: From Basic Logic to Practical Systems
description: This expert talk systematically traced the evolution of digital design, navigating the critical transition from the theoretical elegance of Boolean algebra and fundamental logic gates to the sophisticated integration of complex practical systems. By bridging the gap between discrete combinational and sequential components—such as flip-flops and finite state machines—and modern high-density architectures like FPGAs and SoCs, the session illuminated how abstract binary logic is synthesized into functional hardware. We concluded by addressing the pragmatic engineering constraints of the contemporary industry, specifically emphasizing the roles of Hardware Description Languages (HDL), power dissipation, and propagation delay in transforming rudimentary circuits into high-performance, real-world digital solutions.

title: Expert Talk: Space Talk Series
description:
The V.T. Patel Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, as part of its ongoing "Space Talk Series", organized an insightful expert talk featuring Dr. Sonam Jitarwal, a distinguished scientist from the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL). The session aimed to bridge the gap between classroom electronics and the high-reliability engineering required for interplanetary exploration.

Dr. Jitarwal provided a deep dive into the specialized sensors and instrumentation payloads carried by planetary landers and orbiters. She discussed the extreme environmental constraints—such as radiation, vacuum, and temperature fluctuations—that engineers must account for during the design phase. The talk also covered the role of ECE engineers in signal processing and data transmission from deep space back to Earth stations.

title: Fluid Mechanics Project Competition
description:
The CHAMOS Matrusanstha Department of Mechanical Engineering organized a Fluid Mechanics Project Competition for 4th semester B.Tech students on 4th April 2026 from 09:10 AM to 11:10 AM. The event aimed to enhance conceptual understanding through practical implementation and provide a platform for showcasing innovative fluid mechanics projects.

A total of 48 groups comprising 93 students participated enthusiastically. Students developed and demonstrated working models based on concepts such as Bernoulli’s theorem, vortex flow, surface tension, capillary action, hydrostatic law, wind tunnel applications, flow visualization, pipe losses, metacentric height, and buoyancy. These projects effectively connected theoretical knowledge with real-world applications. Projects were evaluated by faculty based on innovation, technical accuracy, functionality, presentation, and problem-solving approach. The Cyclone Dust Collector project secured the Winner position, while Venturi Injector, Peristaltic Pump, and Water Jet Machining projects achieved Runner-up positions. The competition enhanced students’ practical knowledge, analytical thinking, and teamwork skills. It also improved communication, presentation confidence, and encouraged creativity and innovation.

Overall, the event successfully bridged the gap between theory and practice, providing a valuable learning experience and preparing students for future engineering challenges

description: The Math × AI Escape Challenge, organized under the MathForAI Club, was an inter-department technical competition designed to connect linear algebra concepts with practical Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning applications. The event consisted of engaging rounds including a Linear Algebra Escape Room and a Math × AI/ML Code Sprint. In Round 1, teams solved structured mathematical puzzles within a fixed time limit under the theme "AI Lab Lockdown." The top-performing teams qualified for Round 2, where they implemented core AI/ML algorithms such as Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, k-Means, and Decision Trees from scratch without using external libraries. In the final round, participants were required to demonstrate algorithm correctness, explain mathematical foundations, and present their results effectively. The event provided a competitive yet collaborative platform for applying mathematical knowledge to real-world AI problems.
